nombre.titulo: Okaeri is what you say to someone coming home
cuerpo: In Japan, おかえり is what you say when you hear the front door go. It isn't quite a hello; it's closer to I'm glad you're back.
We took the name because that is what we wanted people to feel walking in, the first time as much as the tenth.

It goes on low in the morning and nobody touches it until it's ready. That's the base for the nine ramen on the menu, and for each one you pick how strong you want the broth, mild, medium or strong, and whether you want it spicy.
Around that there are gyoza, bao, tempura, karaage and takoyaki to pick at, curry rice bowls and Japanese desserts.

tempura.desc: To pick at while the ramen comes.

cocina.alergenos: The allergen table is on the last page of the menu.

sitio.titulo: We built the place we wanted to eat in
cuerpo: From the street it's a stone building like the ones either side of it. Inside we fancied doing something else, so we did: lanterns, neon, bunting and walls covered in manga. Most people look up before they sit down.
The bar does cocktails, bubble tea and Japanese and Korean drinks, so you can come just for a drink. And the cabinet of figures is worth a proper look.

redes.titulo: What goes on in here doesn't fit on a website
redes.texto: Steam off the kitchen, bowls the moment they're up, and a Friday night in full swing. Come and find us.

resenas.titulo: Over a thousand reviews on Google, and they mostly say the same thing
